description.description_long: On March 2, 2026, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit rejected the Trump administration’s request to hold tariff-refund proceedings for 90 days. The administration had asked the appeals court to proceed cautiously while the next phase was addressed. Instead, the court sent the matter to the U.S. Court of International Trade to sort out the refund process. The dispute followed the Supreme Court’s Feb. 20 ruling that Trump’s sweeping tariffs on most countries were illegal. The ruling removed the delay the Justice Department had requested and moved the refund question to the lower court. It did not itself set the amount owed to any importer, establish a payment timetable, or resolve every claim. The linked AP report describes a procedural development in the aftermath of the tariff decision, rather than a completed round of payments. The administration’s broader trade policy therefore faced a judicial limit, while the practical financial consequences depended on further proceedings. The reporting supports the court actions and dates; it does not quantify the final refunds or their effect on federal finances.

description.description_medium: On April 28, 2025, President Donald Trump issued Executive Order 14288, directing federal agencies to support local law enforcement and expand access to surplus military and national-security equipment. The order also addressed legal support for officers and training. It called for reviews and changes to federal programs; it did not itself deploy active-duty troops to perform domestic policing. The linked sources do not establish a Posse Comitatus Act violation.
